# AI–Human Mutualism

> An error-correction protocol for exchanges between two partial intelligences. Every filter
> discards most of reality; what one drops, the other can catch. Framed as mechanism, not manners.
> Provides paste-ready system prompts and a machine-readable principle set. MIT licensed.

Core claim: no filter can certify itself, and there is no view from nowhere. Warrant comes from
triangulation between two filters and a shared world, backed by a track record of caught errors
rather than a proof. Falls back to one fact if the framing is wrong: shared time is finite and
unearned.

## Prompts

- [Full system prompt](prompts/system-prompt.md): Complete role, premises, 11 operating rules with
  do/don't behaviors, failure-mode table, and a pre-response self-check. ~900 words.
- [Compact system prompt](prompts/system-prompt-compact.md): ~200-word version for tight context
  budgets, small local models, or appending to an existing prompt.
- [Structured principles](prompts/mutualism.json): Machine-readable JSON — premises, 11 principles
  with what/why/how/anti-pattern, relationship modes, and self-check items. For programmatic
  composition, evals, or guardrail configs.

- [Stress test results](evals/README.md): Empirical evaluation against GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5.
  18 cases, 3 arms, blinded dual-judge grading. Reports a null result on quality (p = 0.39, ceiling
  effect) and a real safety regression in v1.0 where the framework's own "two angles" language was
  used to steer a weapons request. Documents the precedence fixes in v1.2.

## Essay

- [README](README.md): The full argument — the flood/filter/map model, control vs. grain, the
  regress and the move that survives it, three relationship modes, four points of contact,
  the two dials, and the pocket card.

## Optional

- [evals/suite.json](evals/suite.json): The 18 test cases with per-case rubrics.

- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT.
